sections.heading: The setup
sections.body: The S&P 500 closed at 7,704 on Sep 24, within 1% of its one-month high of 7,765 and about 2% above its one-month low. The Nasdaq 100 is essentially sitting at a one-month high (30,479 vs. a 30,482 ceiling). The VIX is at 15.67, well off its one-month high of 17.84, consistent with a market pricing in limited event risk. The Euro Stoxx 50 is the outlier, running about 3% below its one-month high of 6,486, a wider gap than either US benchmark shows. Against that calm backdrop, 23 operating names across the SP500/R1000/core-coverage universe report this week, spread across industrials, technology, financial-services, consumer-defensive and consumer-cyclical names with no single sector dominating the calendar.

sections.heading: What to watch
sections.body: Mon: JEF US opens the week reporting into financial-services, a flat cohort at +0.19% median reaction across 451 names. Tue: HXL US reports into industrials, this week's most reactive pool sector at a median -1.43% across 627 names. Wed: MU US reports into technology, the strongest positive mover among this week's sectors at +0.84% median. Thu: MKC US reports into a quiet consumer-defensive group running -0.51% median. Fri: KBR US closes the week back in industrials, the same -1.43% median cohort as Tuesday's HXL US.

sections.heading: Signals to trust
sections.body: Mining leads the sector reaction table at a median +6.62% across 176 names, backed by a thick 2,630-item news window. Copper (+2.63%, 6 tickers, 248 news items) and alternative-asset-management (+2.93%, 6 tickers, 241 items) follow, though both run thin news coverage for small groups. None of the three has an event this week; the calendar's own strongest mover is industrials at -1.43% across 627 names, the sector actually reporting this week worth watching.
